pencereler.0-5: Holding in freezing rain, a turboprop suddenly rolled over. It crashed into a field
pencereler.5-12: in Indiana, and sixty eight people were killed. Ice had built up on its wings. Its de-icing boots cracked
pencereler.12-20: off ice at the front. But large droplets froze just behind them. That ridge disturbed the airflow over the ailerons. The controls
pencereler.20-30: snatched, and the plane rolled. Icing certification later expanded to cover these droplets.

segmentler.metin: American Eagle Flight 4184 rolled over and crashed while holding in freezing rain.
It took only a ridge of ice forming behind the wing's de-icing boots.
So how could a ridge of ice forming behind the wing's de-icing boots do this?

The answer is supercooled large droplets forming ice beyond the protected area, disturbing airflow over the ailerons — and it is why icing certification was expanded to cover large supercooled droplets.
